newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Police open investigation into Kiwi Air collapse.
newsitem.headline: Police open investigation into Kiwi Air collapse.

text.p: Police said on Wednesday they had opened an investigation into the collapse of budget carrier Kiwi International Airlines.
Kiwi collapsed last September owing around NZ$5 million to customers who had paid for tickets and more than $3 million to trade and other creditors.
"As a result of documents that were forwarded to us by another government department, we are conducting an investigation," said Detective Inspector Rex Miller of Hamilton police.

He said police became involved prior to Christmas. They had interviewed Kiwi boss Ewan Wilson and would speak to him again if necessary. Miller would not reveal the focus of the police investigation or say whether there was any suspicion of fraud.
The Commerce Ministry is conducting its own inquiry into whether any mismanagement surrounded the failure of Kiwi Air.
